text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King leaves for U.S. on Monday.
- King tells Kabariti government to press ahead with its programme. No change or reshuffle for some time to come. Parliament to be convened for regular session on November 11.
- King assures ex-servicemen of attention to their needs.
- King Hussein to take part in Washington summit. Intensive talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Egyptian Prsident Hosni Mubarak to reach joint outlook.
- King tells ex-servicemen armed forces is a school for good citizenship.

- Jordan to reduce custom tarrifs on cars by 50 per cent over next four years. Value Added Tax (VAT) to become main revenue earner for treasury. There is need to amend the VAT law to prevent tax evasion.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti to go to Muscat next week to dicsuss bilateral ties and Arab-Arab relations.
- King Hussein orders government to send emergency medical supplies to Palestinian Authority.
- Intensive contacts between Hussein. Mubarak and Arafat to agree on common outlook.
- King says army shall remain the shield that protects nation.
- Head of parliament's public freedoms committee expects special pardon for 40 prisoners.
- Jordan signs vocational training agreement with Bahrain.
